newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian president sees risk staying out of NATO.
newsitem.headline: Austrian president sees risk staying out of NATO.

text.p: President Thomas Klestil said on Sunday it could be risky for neutral Austria to stay out of international security structures and called for frank discussion on the issue of NATO entry.
Speaking on state television, Klestil said it was in Austria's interest to extend the zone of security and peace rather than remain on the edge of it.
"Staying out of the security community could have fatal consequences for us in the future."

The coalition government of Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party remain split over the issue, with the former traditionally in favour of remaining neutral and the latter openly backing NATO entry.
The conservatives are opposed to the idea of a referendum while Chancellor Viktor Klima's Social Democrats insist the Austrian people must decide on whether to abandon neutrality.

Conservative Klestil said Austria's long cherished neutral status could be abolished by simply amending the constitution. But if the government decided to hold a referendum, he said he would certainly decree one.

The government is preparing a report on options for possible NATO membership. Klestil said the issue must be represented "with openness, transparency and without taboos", but that it was inextricably linked with neutrality.

The Alpine nation enshrined neutrality in its constitution in 1955 at the insistence of Russia, whose troops, together with those of France, Britain and the United States, occupied Austria after World War Two.
Klestil also spoke out strongly against any delay or toning down of the introduction of the European common currency, saying this would be a big setback for Austria.
A small country like Austria would be better able to meet the challenges "if we are part of a community with ... the euro in a market which is bigger than all other markets," he said.
